liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls the Dark Star a true beauty and a personal favourite; Dark Star was spacey and lovely, with flares fired into the darkening sky [5][6][14][16]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Someone, possibly Pig, makes odd tuning noises in the middle of The Other One; The Dark Star into Other One stretch is called as good as it gets, a tangible display of the band's power [9][13]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Lovelight among the tour's best, perhaps in its top five; The Lovelight into Goin' Down the Road into Not Fade Away sequence contains exceptional jams [9][11]
- **Sing Me Back Home** (1 review): After the intense Other One, Sing Me Back Home feels like church [13]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Garcia hammers the wah-wah pedal at the start of Not Fade Away [9]

## The recordings

- **gd72-05-07.sbd-aud.clugston.9193.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 32 songs; 262 min; rated 4.53/5 by 34 [1]. Said about its sound: Not the best-sounding show, but the playing is inventive in the spirit of Europe '72; Sound is a little sketchy at first, then settles; The first six or so songs sound very poor, then the quality clears up [5][12][14][16]
- **gd1972-05-07.155550.aud.sirmick.flac16**: audience recording; 29 songs; 232 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1972-05-07.133598.sbd.set1.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 13 songs; 95 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1972-05-07.140896.sbd.2p.betty.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: soundboard; 7 songs; 75 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was there, sitting beneath the sound tower during the Dark Star [5]
- During the first set, the smell from the toilets drifted to the stage, and Bob asked the crowd what they were smoking [6]
- An electric sign displayed a 'happy' message during the show, at a farm site near Wigan [6]
- Elvis Costello recalls standing in the mud in a soaked poncho at this show [7]
- Costello was moved most by the band's touching, sad ballads rather than Dark Star [7]
- Donovan played in the early afternoon while drizzle still fell on the exhausted, damp crowd [8]
- A firework display took place during Set II, audible on this tape but not on the soundboard [2]
- New Riders of the Purple Sage opened the show [2]
- Sugar Magnolia through Not Fade Away forms a whole second amazing set in itself [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-05-07.sbd-aud.clugston.9193.sbeok.shnf**: source: Discs 3 & 4 are supplied from a Master Soundboard Reel > DAT source [1]. Also: Discs 1 and 2 come from multiple audience sources; discs 3 and 4 from the master soundboard reel; Discs 1 and 2 compile several audience sources; discs 3 and 4 come from a master soundboard reel transferred to DAT [1][16]
- **gd1972-05-07.155550.aud.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Simon Phillips, unknown; transferred by Sirmick; source: Multiple audience sources [2]. Also: Compiled from three sources; Simon Phillips' master covers all of Set II, and only one taper is known [2]
- **gd1972-05-07.133598.sbd.set1.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (10 inch - 1/2 track) -> Dat/48k [3]
- **gd1972-05-07.140896.sbd.2p.betty.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Betty Cantor and Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Partial Set 2 Source Info: Betty's Master Soundboard Reel > PCM > PCM (14-bit)(Sony L-750ESX-HFB tape); Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD >… [4]

## Art and photos

- Photo by Caine Schneider (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 5/7/72 Bickershaw Festival, Wigan, England](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26860491615/) [18]
- Photo by Boo (All rights reserved): [Bickershaw Festival 1972](https://www.flickr.com/photos/14881078@N06/7131687707/) [19]
